title: The Name that remains
hookLine: kings and their enemies pass; the ninth Guru names what stays

lines: AN OLD PHOTOGRAPH IN A BOX.
cards: Everyone in this photograph is gone now. It came out of a box in a closet: a wedding, maybe, or a family on a porch. The porch is gone.
The clothes, the car, the town as it looked. On the back, in faded pencil, somebody wrote down who they were. Of everything in that picture, the writing has outlasted the people.
Yesterday the ninth Guru called the world a dream. Today, near the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib, he names what doesn't drain away when you wake.

teach.b: Two saloks, side by side, paraphrased. The first: Ram has gone, and Ravan has gone, though he had a great family; nothing is fixed, says Nanak, the world is like a dream.
Ram and Ravan, the hero and the enemy of the Ramayana, a story Hindus hold sacred. Even the kings of that story, on both sides, passed from the earth. Then the turn.

teach.h: THE NAME, THE HOLY, THE GURU REMAIN.
teach.b: The second salok: the Name has remained; the holy ones have remained; the Guru, the Lord of the world, has remained. And a question: says Nanak, who in this world has truly repeated the Guru's mantra?
So here's what stays. Not palaces, families or kingdoms. The Name, which Sikhs understand as the presence of God, remembered and repeated.
The holy ones, the company of people who live that remembering. And the Guru, the Lord, the source of it all. The pencil on the photograph lasts a while, then fades too.
The Name in this salok isn't writing on paper.
It's what a life is pointed toward.
When Sikhs remember the Name, saying Waheguru, singing the hymns, keeping it under the breath through a working day, they're touching the one thing the Guru says isn't part of the dream.
That closing question is honest, not proud. The Guru doesn't claim everyone remembers; he asks who has. Some readers hear a quiet invitation in it: be one who does, once more today.
If a loss is heavy on you right now, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US, call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.

how: These saloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur are read near the close of a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, and Sikhs practice naam simran, remembering the Name, by repeating Waheguru and singing gurbani.

games.q: what does “the name that remains” mean?
o: the Name, the holy and the Guru, which last when all else passes
a family name carved on a stone so it is never forgotten
the Guru's signature, Nanak, written at the end of each hymn

games.q: what passes, and what remains: tap the pairs.
p: who in this world has repeated it? asks Nanak

s: the salok says even Ravan, with his great family, has gone
nothing is fixed; the world is like a dream.
the salok claims everyone remembers the Name
it asks who in this world has truly repeated the Guru's mantra.
the Name in the salok means a written name on paper
it's the presence of God, remembered and repeated.

games.q: everything in the old photograph is gone: the people, the porch, the town. according to the ninth Guru's salok, what's still standing?
o: the Name, the holy ones and the Guru.
games.why: the Name has remained, the holy ones have remained, the Guru, the Lord of the world, has remained.

practice: Let the passing things of your day drift by, the inbox, the dishes, the news, like pictures in a closet box.

Then come back to one thing that stays: if you pray, repeat Waheguru quietly once on each breath; if not, choose one word for what lasts for you and return to it whenever the mind wanders. Once more, and once more.

wordCard.voice: The Name that remains. When kings, families and kingdoms pass, the ninth Guru's salok says the Name, the holy ones and the Guru remain. Today's word.

orig.note: the Name: in Sikh teaching, the presence of God, remembered and repeated; the salok says it remains.

carryVoice: Your line: it remains. Whatever passes, the Name still stays. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Salok Mahala 9, Ang 1429 (Ram gaio Ravan gaio: Ram and Ravan have gone)
Guru Granth Sahib, Salok Mahala 9, Ang 1429 (naam rahio sadhu rahio rahio gur gobind)
